correctness.rationale: The weighted bipartite tree enumerator gives exact signed Walsh coefficients, with zero iff an even shore has balanced signs. The nonzero frequency support factors. Krawtchouk duality and the generating polynomial (1-u^2)^r give an exact absolute sum and hence Phi(2r). The projection kernel factors over shores, and averaging over all translations proves the norm is minimal over all real or complex projections. Independent enumerations for six sizes and exact Krawtchouk identities for shore sizes through sixteen corroborate, but the infinite conclusion rests on the analytical argument. The limiting leading constant follows from Stirling.

originality.rationale: The named 2015 weighted enumerator already implies the signed Walsh multiplier, and the 2023 general projection theorem already implies translation-averaging minimality. The asserted new claim is the closed sharp product Phi(m)Phi(n) specifically for the full odd-degree vertex-profile kernel of every K_{m,n}, proved by an exact middle-Hamming-layer Krawtchouk absolute-sum evaluation. Inspected prior full texts state neither this explicit vertex-parity range-projection constant nor its exponential versus asymptotically vanishing-nullity conclusion. A bounded search cannot certify global priority.

value.rationale: Odd-degree vertex sets are a canonical coarse observation of spanning trees. The exact least amplification for projection onto recoverable signals is a motivated information-recovery invariant.
